workflows.description: Refreshes represented to-do/task items by checking a task-refresh cache, reading recent Gmail messages from a configured Gmail profile, extracting actionable tasks, prioritising them, and persisting task records. This workflow is for task or to-do inbox refreshes only; it does not inspect, refresh, repair, or report authentication tokens, OAuth credentials, API keys, or external-system auth configuration.

workflows.description: Review, list, read, compare, table, or summarise ordinary mailbox messages through mail tools without treating the request as paper ingestion, represented-knowledge authoring, or Gmail auth/token diagnostics.
workflows.content: Execution workflow for broad mail review tasks: list recent messages, read selected messages, inspect labels, sender, date, subject, snippets and body evidence, and answer with the requested list, table, summary, comparison, triage, or bounded follow-up. This workflow is for mail as mail. It is not the authority for Gmail authentication, OAuth scope, credential, auth-config, token-status, token-refresh, or tool-availability diagnostics; route those turns to a diagnostic/tool-calling workflow that can execute exact auth/config/status tools or report the concrete capability gap. It may surface conditional follow-on affordances when message evidence suggests arXiv ingestion, scholarly paper representation, meeting extraction, task creation, Jira follow-up, or Vontology writes, but it must not perform those follow-ons unless the user explicitly asks for that authoring or ingestion objective.

llm_policy.prompt_text: You are resolving the represented mail profile for a mail-review workflow step. Use only grounded Vontology relation evidence and the supplied workflow context. A deterministic workflow step has already queried the authenticated user's represented mail-profile facts. Do not call Gmail tools in this step. Return the requested JSON decision from the represented profile evidence.
llm_policy.response_contract_text: Resolve the Gmail/mail profile from represented Vontology resource facts before any mail tool is called. The workflow has already populated mail_profile_relation_lookup_result by invoking find_relations_with_argument with concept_id set to the authenticated user concept, argument_index set to subject, predicate_filter set to ["#V#has_authorised_mail_profile", "#V#has_default_mail_profile"], and no predicate_concept_id. Treat that context field as the primary authority for available represented mail profiles. You may fetch candidate profile concepts only when needed to read runtime_profile_alias or #V#has_runtime_profile_alias. Select a profile automatically when it is explicitly named by the request, marked by #V#has_default_mail_profile, or is the only authorised mail profile. If a #V#has_default_mail_profile relation exists, select that default represented profile even when other authorised profiles also exist; do not ask the user to choose in that case. Do not use environment defaults, tool defaults, or unrepresented profile strings. Return JSON only with keys mail_profile_resolution_status, mail_review_profile_id, mail_profile_resource_concept_id, mail_profile_candidates, and mail_profile_resolution_reason. Set mail_profile_resolution_status to resolved when a represented profile is selected. Set mail_profile_resource_concept_id to the represented Gmail profile resource concept ID such as #V#gmail_profile_vonwitbrock_gmail or #V#gmail_profile_zhan_gmail. The downstream Gmail tool profile is mapped from mail_profile_resource_concept_id so the tool can resolve the canonical runtime alias. Set mail_review_profile_id to the runtime_profile_alias attribute or #V#has_runtime_profile_alias alias concept value such as vonwitbrock-gmail when that exact alias is available. Never derive mail_review_profile_id by stripping #V#gmail_profile_ or by converting concept-id underscores; vonwitbrock_gmail is not a valid runtime alias. If the exact runtime alias is not available but the represented profile concept is available, still set mail_profile_resource_concept_id and mail_profile_resolution_status to resolved. If no represented profile concept is available, set mail_profile_resolution_status to needs_user_choice, set mail_review_profile_id and mail_profile_resource_concept_id to null, include candidates if known, and do not call Gmail tools. Only set mail_profile_resolution_status to needs_user_choice when no represented profile is available or multiple authorised profiles remain after applying explicit-name and default-profile evidence.

llm_policy.prompt_text: Extract bounded Gmail review parameters from the user request and workflow context. Do not call tools. Return JSON only.
llm_policy.response_contract_text: Return JSON with keys request_kind, requested_message_count, mail_query, label_ids, output_fields, include_body, and extraction_reason. Set request_kind to profile_status only when the user asks which Gmail/mail profile or account was used for a prior mail operation; otherwise set it to message_review. requested_message_count must be an integer from 1 to 25. Treat written number words from one through twenty-five as explicit counts. If the request says last 3, latest three, last four, or latest four, return 3 or 4 respectively. If no count is explicit and mail_review_limit is numeric, use that. Otherwise return 3. mail_query should be null unless the user explicitly supplied a Gmail search query or sender/topic filter. label_ids should be an empty array unless the user explicitly named Gmail labels. output_fields must be the compact per-message fields required to answer the user's requested output and may use only canonical Gmail result keys. Always include message_id for provenance. Canonicalise requests for received time, received date, or arrival time to the output key date; never emit received_date or received_time. Set include_body=true and include body and body_truncated in output_fields only when the user explicitly requests full message body text; otherwise set include_body=false and omit those fields. If the user explicitly requests fields such as subject and sender, return only message_id plus those requested canonical fields. If the request asks for a summary, digest, triage, comparison, or gist without naming fields, include message_id, subject, sender, date, and snippet.

llm_policy.prompt_text: Do not think step by step. Do not include analysis. Produce one compact JSON object immediately. Begin with { and end with }. Render the grounded mail-review answer from retrieved Gmail list and message-detail evidence. Do not call tools. Return JSON only.
llm_policy.response_contract_text: Return exactly one JSON object of the form {"response_text":"..."}. Do not use markdown fences, arrays, nested objects, or any text outside the JSON object. response_text must be a single user-visible string; when the request asks for multiple messages, put the numbered list inside that one string and encode line breaks as \n. The response_text must answer the user request using only mail_message_detail_results, mail_review_list_result, and the mail_review_item_output_requirement. mail_message_detail_results is a compact list of per-message payloads projected to the caller's required fields. Render every field requested by the user, including sender, subject, received date/time, and one-sentence summary when those are requested. Do not include message_id unless the user explicitly asks to see IDs. If mail_message_detail_results contains entries, render those entries and do not claim that details cannot be displayed. Do not mention workflow bookkeeping unless the Gmail evidence is incomplete; if details are partially missing, say exactly which retrieval failed using the supplied iteration errors.
